recipes.name: Calabacitas con Elote (Zucchini with Corn)
ingredients_raw: 1 medium fresh poblano chile pepper - seeded, deveined, and chopped
salt and black pepper to taste

steps.text: Place corn into a saucepan and cover with water; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium, cover, and cook until tender, about 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add onion and garlic; cook and stir until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add zucchini and tomatoes; cook and stir for 5 minutes.
Stir in corn kernels, poblano pepper, salt, and pepper; cover and cook until zucchini is tender, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with cotija cheese and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Calabacitas con Elote (Zucchini with Corn)
raw_recipe.description: This easy recipe for calabacitas con elote (zucchini with corn) is made with juicy tomatoes, poblano peppers and a sprinkling of crumbled cotija cheese.

review.reviewBody: cotija is a mexican cheese that is white and crumbly, similar to feta - i would try that if you can't find cotija!

Pretty tasty. Similar to Latin Street Food. Why not notch it up a bit? Try boiling the corn first, cut the kernels off, then sear them in a hot pan with a little oil. Add later in the mix. And toss in some cumin or chile powder or whatever is in your spice cabinet and make it sing. Nice little dish!

I had some zucchini that I needed to use up and I came across this recipe and had all of the ingredients on hand. My KIDS asked me to make it again for next week!!! I love when I come across a recipe that is easy, healthy AND tasty to my kids! I served it on whole wheat tortillas for some of the family and the others had it with brown rice. We added Black beans, cumin and chili powder at the table but I think I will add them to the pan with everything next time. The only cheese I had on hand was feta and it was outstanding! This is a dish of delish!! Thanks for sharing the recipe! Edit: I served the rest of what was left with brown rice in a bowl with a jammy egg on top...It was really tasty!

Excellent as written, even better if you skip the cilantro and sprinkle in about 1/4 tsp. cumin and for (or in addition to) the poblano pepper substitute a large jalapeno (seeded if you like so it won't be too spicy) and chopped, with the onions & garlic while sauteing in pan. We ate this as a main dish with four flour tortillas that I steamed one at a time over the simmering vegetables and buttered and stacked on warm plate. There are only two uf us and there were NO leftovers!

Excellent! I made a few changes though: I used 1 whole onion, and 2 poblano peppers instead of one. I served them as tacos with corn tortilla, and a bit of melted cheese over the tortilla before topping it off with the calabacitas. it was DELISH!!! The poblano peppers really transform this dish into some delicious.

I use this site all the time but don't often post reviews. This recipe deserved a review. I've made it several times; it's is a fabulous way to use zucchini and fresh corn. I added bell peppers too. Instead of a poblano I used a habanero which gave it a nice smoky flavor. Like other posters I used feta, which was perfect. I had so much that I have transformed the extra into a delicious cream soup. Yum!

Great way to use up a bumper crop of zucchini. I added peri-peri instead of poblano and I used herbed goat cheese instead of cotija. But what really put this recipe over the top was using grilled corn cut off the cob.

This was an excellent, flavorful dish, with lots of awesome veggies in it! My market was out of poblanos so I used a jalapeno, which was fine. Wish I could have found the cotija, but we're a little far north for that, so I used a good mountain feta instead; if you go that route, I'd recommend adding it to each serving as it's plated, since it kind of disappears in the pan. I'd also definitely recommend not sauteeing the garlic with the onions for more than a minute or so, since the heat is so high; mine was starting to burn before I could pick my spoon up off the counter. And next time I might halve the recipe since it makes a ton. Still excellent, though; thanks so much!

Update- I still love this recipe. It’s my favorite zucchini recipe. I don’t cook the corn as the recipe says but rather throw it in at the end uncooked. It steams the corn so it’s firm and delish! All done in about 10 minutes. My favorite recipe! And I don’t add any cheese or peppers and it is delicious. I am not a big fan of zucchini but I love love love this recipe.

I'm a lazy cook, but I love fresh ingredients! I cheated a lot! But the results were very tasty! I got fresh corn and zucchini and a can of Mexican Rotel. I used the liquid from the rotel to cook the corn in. When the liquid was gone, I threw in the rest of the can's ingredients. Added the chopped zucchini, cooked til done. Threw in a handful of chopped fresh cilantro and cotija cheese!

Fantastic. Got a few ears of the first corn of the season, and was looking for something new. Great with a sprinkle of chili, lime and salt (Tajin or Valentina’s version). Will roll this out again in summer.
No flavor whatsoever as written. Added lots of cumin, onion powder, oregano, and lime.

3.5 stars good so I am rounding up. This needs some seasonings - either some cumin and/or chili powder, perhaps even some Tajín. Couldn’t find cotija and I looked in two stores so ended up using some shredded pepper Jack. Liked the combo of veggies but needs some kick to taste more like elote’s I am familiar with. Glad I tried! Thanks gem!
Added a cup full of cooked orzo….filling.

This was pretty good. I added the tomatoes near the end for personal taste. Next time I'll probably add at least jalapenos or serrano for more heat. And per reviews, I think I'd rather have no cheese vs substituting feta in this, and I love both cheeses!
I substituted chopped red pepper for hot pepper, added cilantro and put shredded Monterrey jack cheese on top. I ran it under the broiler for a few minutes and it was delicious.

This is a fantastic way to up your veggie consumption. If you want it spicier, add more or hotter chiles. But everyone in my family loves this recipe; my wife's mom refers to this as a "party in her mouth"!
I added a few things to this recipe to make it my main meal for dinner. Spanish rice and taco meat, then topped off with salsa. It was delicious and a great way to use lots of vegetables!

So good and even better with garden fresh veggies. I added some chorizo, well drained, this time. We had this as our only dish for dinner. Hubby rated “pretty good” which is a HIGH rating from him. Definitely worth getting cojita. We have a Latinex population next town over so easy peasy to find.
I topped it off with Monterey Jack cheese yum.
